*Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 10.1) is a canonical text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, forming a subsection within the *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral]. The text systematically treats conditional relations through the matrix combination of the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*) and the root dyad (*hetuduka*) [SuttaCentral].
In terms of textual parallels and reuse, machine analysis by DharmaNexus records 1,407 matching passages shared across 113 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive internal overlaps occur with other combinatory treatments of triads and dyads within the *Paṭṭhāna*, led by *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1) with 153 matches (including §2.1_0–4.1_6 ↔ §44.0.2–51.1), *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 22.1) with 54 matches, and *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2) with 70 matches [DharmaNexus]. High-similarity passages are also shared with another *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* section (Patthana 16.1; §0.2–4.1_0 ↔ §0.2–4.1_0 with 0.9 similarity), *Kusalattika, Sahetukaduka* (Patthana 10.2), and *Hetuduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 9.1) [DharmaNexus].
Beyond the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects cross-language alignments with Sanskrit Buddhist Abhidharma literature, identifying five matches with Vimalamitra's *Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti* (achieving a top plausibility score of 75, e.g., §3.1_1 ↔ §3127) [DharmaNexus].
